'''Lawrence 'Lawrie' Dring''' (4 July 1931&nbsp;–  6 September 2012) was a British [[Scouter]] who was one of the founding members of the [[Baden-Powell Scouts' Association]] (BPSA) and of the [[World Federation of Independent Scouts]] (WFIS).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.bpsa-bc.org/i-history.htm |title=History of the Baden-Powell Scouts Associations |access-date=3 April 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725100853/http://www.bpsa-bc.org/i-history.htm |archive-date=25 July 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was President of the BPSA at the time of his death.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.traditionalscouting.co.uk/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=935:gone-home-bob&catid=85:public-messages&Itemid=57 |title=Gone Home – Lawrie (Bob) Dring |work=Baden-Powell Scouts' Association |date=6 September 2012 |access-date=9 September 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121117193620/http://www.traditionalscouting.co.uk/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=935%3Agone-home-bob&catid=85%3Apublic-messages&Itemid=57 |archive-date=17 November 2012 }}</ref>

Dring was born on Dundee railway station, one of twin boys.  At the time of his birth his mother was attempting to return to Leeds to ensure that the boys were born Yorkshiremen.  Although born in Scotland, with a Scottish father and proud to call himself a Scot, his birth was registered in Leeds.{{CN|date=November 2021}}  His brother was killed as an adult in a car accident.

After leaving school, Dring worked for Fisons Chemicals, until joining Allied Colloids in 1973.  He also ran his own company, Dring Associates, which dealt with the disposal of hazardous waste.<ref>[http://www.dringassociates.co.uk/index.html Dring Associates website]</ref>

In 1947, Dring was a soldier in the [[British Army]] stationed in [[Wuppertal]], Germany when a colleague asked him to become a [[Cub Scout]] leader. After returning from his [[national service]] he joined the Leeds District of [[The Boy Scout Association]], serving on the executive until the adoption of [[The Chief Scouts' Advance Party Report]].  Disagreeing with the direction of the association, he resigned and helped form the [[Baden-Powell Scouts' Association]] and the [[World Federation of Independent Scouts]].

In addition to serving a term as chief commissioner of the B-PSA, and later as president, he continued to volunteer as a Scouter for 1st Yorkshire Baden-Powell Scouts Troop. He visited Canada, the United States, Germany, South Africa and Australia.<ref>[http://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/news/community/obituaries/lawrence-dring-1-4950901 Lawrence Dring, obituary, Yorkshire Post]</ref>

Dring's funeral took place on 21 September 2012 at the Holy Trinity Church at [[Rothwell, West Yorkshire|Rothwell]].  His coffin was met by an honour guard of Scouts and leaders from several Scout associations and was carried by Scouts from First Yorkshire B-P Scout Group.  The service was conducted by the Reverend Jeremy Trigg, who had been one of Dring's [[Wolf Cubs]].  The committal took place at [[Stanley, West Yorkshire|Stanley]] Cemetery.
